readme:
# CodeLLDB

A native debugger powered by LLDB: debug C, C++, Rust and other compiled languages from Run and Debug. The debug adapter and LLDB come with the extension — nothing to install on the machine.

On first activation the extension downloads its platform package (about 30 MB) from the CodeLLDB releases on GitHub and installs it; the progress shows as "Acquiring CodeLLDB platform package". Without network access the debugger can't start.

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version and verified to work in Diode.

## What works in Diode

`launch.json` configurations of type `lldb` with `preLaunchTask` (build with `gcc -g`), F5, breakpoints in the gutter (F9, click), stepping (F10, F11, Shift+F11), Continue, Restart and Stop. VARIABLES, WATCH, CALL STACK and BREAKPOINTS fill from the session, the current line is highlighted, and the Debug Console evaluates LLDB commands and `?expression`. `"terminal": "integrated"` runs the program in the integrated terminal, so it reads your input. `"request": "attach"` with `${command:pickProcess}` offers the running processes. CodeLLDB's own Modules and Excluded Callers views sit in Run and Debug.

## What does not

Webview output (`debugger.display_html`) is not shown — a terminal can't draw HTML. There is no disassembly view. The extension's language model tools are ignored — Diode has no language models.
